tasks.title: Docs: explain the supported g2o package path and EOL boundary
tasks.outcome: A new user can distinguish a missing libg2o dependency from an incompatible source-built g2o API and return to the maintained Humble or Jazzy package path.
acceptance: A reader can identify whether the failure is dependency resolution or a C++ API mismatch.
Humble and Jazzy are the only maintained distributions claimed.
The card links to the product support boundary.
The text shows rosdep resolve libg2o and a supported binary-package check.
No hardware support or build-success claim is added without evidence.

tasks.title: Docs: add a three-check recovery card for an empty /map or viewer
tasks.outcome: A first-run user can separate missing PointCloud2 input, an empty sampled frame, a disconnected TF path, and a viewer-only problem before asking for support.
non_goals: promise support for an untested sensor
acceptance: The card provides one check each for a live PointCloud2 input, a non-empty sampled frame_id, and a connected TF path.
Each command names the expected observation and one next action.
Placeholder topic and frame names are visibly marked for replacement.
The card distinguishes no map messages from a wrong viewer topic or fixed frame.
The card does not ask a user to upload a map, bag, or location-bearing log.
The fixed public demo remains the first control experiment.

tasks.title: Docs: explain why an Odometry topic does not guarantee odom -> base_link TF
tasks.outcome: A user can tell the difference between a nav_msgs/msg/Odometry message, a missing odom-to-base transform, and a stale transform that causes extrapolation.
acceptance: The card explains that an Odometry publisher does not necessarily broadcast the corresponding transform.
The Odometry header, odom-to-base TF availability, and transform freshness each have an explicit check.
Frame direction and placeholder names are explicit.
A missing transform and an extrapolation problem end in different safe next actions.
The card does not recommend suppressing TF warnings as a fix or copy a third-party broadcaster implementation.

tasks.title: Docs: add the minimal checklist for adapting another PointCloud2 LiDAR
tasks.outcome: A user adapting a sensor can verify the generic PointCloud2 input contract and reach a controlled first run without guessing vendor-specific tuning or extrinsics.
non_goals: claim support for hardware that has not passed a recipe
acceptance: The checklist covers the PointCloud2 topic, non-empty frame, static extrinsic, timestamps, scan period, and min/max range.
Every checklist item has one observation command or configuration field.
Public launch arguments show how to remap the topic and frames.
Vendor names remain examples and are not added to the supported matrix.
Success means ready for a controlled first run rather than accuracy validated.
The text explicitly rejects guessing an extrinsic and links to the sensor-support issue form.

tasks.title: Preflight: fail clearly when sampled sensor messages have an empty frame_id
tasks.outcome: Readable sensor samples whose frame_id values are all empty produce a clear failed preflight check, while unavailable sampling remains advisory.
acceptance: Readable messages with only empty frame IDs produce a clear failed pointcloud_frame_id or imu_frame_id check.
A sample-reader failure does not masquerade as an empty-frame failure.
Existing mismatch, changing-frame, and stable-frame cases keep their current status.
The regression test needs no rosbag, hardware, network, or generated map.
